c.tagline: Georgia's palm-fringed Black Sea resort of casinos, quirky towers and subtropical rain.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmarked and unmetered — agree the fare before getting in, or use Bolt or Yandex Go for a fixed app price.

emergency.note: 112 is Georgia's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire, with English-speaking operators available.

avoid.reason: Watch for inflated bills at casinos, strip clubs and some seafront bars, plus petty theft on the crowded beach in peak summer.

hood_desc: The historic core around Europe Square and the Piazza, with pastel 19th-century facades, cafes, wine bars and the main sights; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
The green promenade strip along Batumi Boulevard, lined with beachfront hotels, bike paths, fountains and the Ali & Nino moving statue; central and lively through the summer.
The modern high-rise quarter at the north end of the boulevard, home to the Alphabet Tower, casinos, clubs and towers like the Sheraton and Hilton; the city's nightlife hub.
A quieter seaside village about 12 km south near the Turkish border, with a pebble beach, the Roman-era Gonio fortress and a relaxed, family-friendly feel.
A calm coastal suburb just north of the center reached by the Argo cable car and marshrutka, with a quieter beach and lower prices; good for a slower base.

water.note: Tap water is generally safe to drink, though many visitors prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Municipal buses run roughly 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM; the Argo cable car operates daytime into the evening (around 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM in summer).
transit.note: Batumi has no metro or tram; a modern municipal bus network plus marshrutka minibuses cover the city, and the Argo cable car links the seafront to the Anuria hilltop. Bolt and Yandex Go fill late-night gaps.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid with the BatumiCard or a contactless bank card on board (around 0.50 GEL); marshrutkas take cash. The cable car has a separate ticket (around 15-20 GEL round trip).

bus: Intercity marshrutkas and buses to Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Turkey
ferry: Batumi Sea Port (cargo, with occasional passenger and cruise calls)
train: Georgian Railway: Batumi-Tbilisi line from Batumi Central, plus summer trains toward Kutaisi and Zugdidi

transit.m: City bus #10 to the center (~20 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving ~10% for good service is appreciated. Some restaurants already add a service charge to the bill.
